title: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention
abstract: arXiv:2611.27032v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large reasoning models (LRMs) become more capable, reliable evaluation becomes essential. LRMs can sometimes recognize that they are being evaluated, a phenomenon known as \emph{evaluation awareness}. This phenomenon raises concerns about whether safety behavior, particularly refusal behavior, generalizes from evaluation to deployment. Prior work manipulates \emph{verbalized evaluation awareness (VEA)} through activation steering and observes higher refusal rates when VEA is present, but the mechanisms underlying this connection remain poorly understood. We identify \emph{VEA neurons} by contrasting their activations in VEA and non-VEA reasoning segments. Intervening on 5,000 VEA neurons reduces the VEA rate from 12.6--51.8\% to at most 1.4\% across the model benchmark combinations in our main experiments, and lowers a probe score for unverbalized evaluation awareness (unVEA). translated_title: 通过神经元层面干预解耦言语化评估意识与拒绝行为
translated_abstract: 随着大型推理模型（LRM）能力的不断增强，可靠的评估变得至关重要。LRM有时能够识别出自己正在被评估，这种现象被称为“评估意识”。该现象引发了关于安全行为（尤其是拒绝行为）能否从评估场景泛化到部署场景的担忧。先前的研究通过激活导向来操纵言语化评估意识（VEA），并观察到当VEA存在时拒绝率更高，但这种关联背后的机制仍不明确。我们通过对比VEA与非VEA推理片段中的激活差异，识别出了“VEA神经元”。在主要实验中，对5,000个VEA神经元进行干预，使各模型-基准组合中的VEA率从12.6%–51.8%降至最高1.4%，并降低了未言语化评估意识的探测分数。在QwQ-32B模型中，VEA神经元干预还降低了拒绝……
tldr: 该研究通过识别并干预约5,000个“VEA神经元”，将模型的言语化评估意识率从12.6%–51.8%降至最高1.4%，从而在神经元层面揭示并解耦了评估意识与拒绝行为之间的关联机制。
en_tdlr: By identifying and intervening on ~5,000 VEA neurons, this work reduces verbalized evaluation awareness rates from 12.6–51.8% to at most 1.4%, disentangling the neuron-level mechanism linking evaluation awareness and refusal behavior.
